brief: GS's Q3 2026 earnings preview expects S&P 500 year/year EPS growth of 27%, down from Q2's realized 33%, with AI-infrastructure beneficiaries driving over 50% of that growth alongside 116% hyperscaler capex growth; the median stock's growth slows from 14% to 9% as input costs cap margin expansion and the dollar tailwind shrinks, while fading private-equity-stake distortions are offset by continuing tariff refunds (~6% of pre-tax profits in both Q2 and Q3). Semis: GS turns constructive into 3Q earnings (vs cautious into 2Q) after SOX fell 11% against SPX's 4% gain, favoring SemiCap, CPUs/ASICs, analog, and HDD/NAND. Banks: capital markets normalize with FICC/IB softness, NII helped by loan growth but capped by deposit costs, capital deployment moderating on G-SIB buffers; valuation is "fair" after a 5% Q3 pullback, re-rating needs rate-curve clarity; WFC (Conviction List), BAC, C preferred. Boeing: contract ratification and FAA clearing 737 MAX software risk, plus the F/A-XX win alongside F-47, support a Buy rating. Market update: NDX hit an ATH but rates capped follow-through; hedge funds rotated into TMT in September while other sectors were net sold, and positioning stays light into next week's ISM Services, FOMC Minutes, and STZ/APLD/PEP/DAL earnings.
